items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Buddy Miller who would get drunk occasionally... Andy told him very nicely to take the rest of the night off... Andy fired Buddy then and there

ctx.x: Andy Kirk was a gentle leader who had once been a baritone sax player in some orchestra around St. Louis or Kansas City, so I was told. He was very patient with the musicians but no one gave him much trouble except Buddy Miller who would get drunk occasionally and could not do his job correctly.

Being new in the band, I knew nothing about this, until one night at the famous "Door", after an intermission, he had met some trampy looking girl in the White Rose bar around the corner from the club on 6th Avenue and gotten drunk and brought this chick back to the club with him. Before the intermission he seemed to be alright, but when he came back, he could hardly stand. Buddy was also a quiet type of fellow and a fine first alto man.
